name: Nigel Oakes

summary.text: Nigel Oakes is the founder of the Behavioural Dynamics Institute and a co-founder of SCL Group, the British parent of Cambridge Analytica. Written evidence to the DCMS Committee from Dr Emma Briant describes the Behavioural Dynamics Institute as a research centre of SCL Group with Oakes as chairman, and quotes Oakes as saying its methodology was being taught across NATO. Brittany Kaiser told the committee Oakes was the SCL co-founder in charge of its defence division, and Christopher Wylie said he believed SCL's defence arm had worked for the Ministry of Defence and DSTL.

sources.title: Written evidence submitted by Dr Emma L Briant (FKN0099)
Written evidence submitted by Dr Emma L Briant (FKN0071)
Oral evidence: Fake news, HC 363, 17 April 2018 (Brittany Kaiser)
Oral evidence: Fake news, HC 363, 27 March 2018 (Christopher Wylie)

facts.claim: Dr Emma Briant's written evidence to the DCMS Committee describes Nigel Oakes as chairman of the Behavioural Dynamics Institute, which she describes as a research centre of SCL Group.
facts.quote: Oakes is Chairman of the Behavioural Dynamics Institute

sources.title: Written evidence submitted by Dr Emma L Briant (FKN0071)

facts.claim: Briant's evidence, drawing on a 2017 interview with Oakes, states that SCL was a government contractor that developed its methodology through the Behavioural Dynamics Institute, and quotes Oakes saying the methodology was being taught across NATO; the DCMS final report recorded that SCL Group was delivering counter-Russian propaganda training for NATO.
facts.quote: is now being taught right away across NATO

sources.title: Written evidence submitted by Dr Emma L Briant (FKN0099)
Disinformation and 'fake news': Final Report, chapter 7: SCL influence in foreign elections

facts.claim: Brittany Kaiser told the DCMS Committee on 17 April 2018 that Oakes, the SCL co-founder in charge of its defence division, had told her the target audience analysis methodology had once been export controlled by the British Government.
facts.quote: That is what I was told by Nigel Oakes, yes.

sources.title: Oral evidence: Fake news, HC 363, 17 April 2018 (Brittany Kaiser)

facts.claim: Christopher Wylie told the DCMS Committee on 27 March 2018 that SCL's defence arm had done work for the Ministry of Defence and, he believed, for DSTL.
facts.quote: has done work for the Ministry of Defence and also, I believe, for DSTL

sources.title: Oral evidence: Fake news, HC 363, 27 March 2018 (Christopher Wylie)

facts.claim: Briant's evidence quotes Oakes as saying that defence staff could not be seen to be getting involved in politics, describing a separation between SCL's defence and political work.
facts.quote: defence staff can't be seen to be getting involved in politics

sources.title: Written evidence submitted by Dr Emma L Briant (FKN0099)

connections.claim: Oakes is described in DCMS Committee evidence as a co-founder of SCL Group who ran its defence division and chaired its research centre, the Behavioural Dynamics Institute.
connections.quote: the co-founder of the SCL Group, who was in charge of our defence division

sources.title: Oral evidence: Fake news, HC 363, 17 April 2018 (Brittany Kaiser)
Written evidence submitted by Dr Emma L Briant (FKN0071)

openQuestions: The Ministry of Defence's reported 2011 commendation of SCL/Oakes could not be found in the sources opened; the MoD link rests on witness evidence.
Oakes's earlier work in Indonesia in the 1990s and the SCL companies' prior names were not sourced beyond Wikipedia and are not recorded.
Did Oakes himself give evidence to the DCMS Committee? None was found.
